title: Illnesses
description: Sicknesses of the rustling waves, from the commonplace to the uncanny - conditions that limit a character rather than a ship.
inPlay: Be careful when making an illness the focus of an arc. Most illnesses are best inflicted on an important or well-liked NPC, a passenger, or a member of the undercrew, so the players deal with the fallout without their own characters being sidelined.

hazards.name: Insulia
hazards.summary: An affectation of wrappings, most often found in mothryn but transmittable to anyone: sufferers compulsively wrap themselves in layer after layer of material, and deaths from overheating and self-crushing are common.

hazards.name: Oskatar's Bones
hazards.summary: The bones stop growing while the body continues to grow physically larger, leaving sufferers burdened and strengthened by their new weight; Oskatar is said to have cured his own case.

hazards.name: Tarak's Lung
hazards.summary: Probably the most common condition on the wildsea, named after the very first sailor of the rustling waves: breathe in too much of the bad air and you end up with it. Symptoms vary wildly, but a wracking cough is common to all cases.

hazards.name: Gilli
hazards.summary: A particularly cruel lung condition in which the lungs labour without clean air and unnatural vapours; sufferers often rely on masks and tanks to live a normal life.

hazards.name: Polypoid Tendrils
hazards.summary: A salt-borne contagion, a throwback to the old pre-verdant seas, that causes suckered tentacles to sprout from exposed skin; the process is slow, excruciating, and begins internally.

hazards.name: Amberblight
hazards.summary: A localized infection that takes hold in a wound or cut and slowly spreads through the host's body, hardening the afflicted flesh as it goes.

hazards.name: The Roving
hazards.summary: A yearning for the open waves that overcomes all else and shreds logic, sense, and responsibility; easily cured by bedrest and manacles if caught early enough.

hazards.name: Unscrewing
hazards.summary: A syndrome of uncontrollable displays of intense magnetic force, caused not by arconautic power but by a gut bacteria picked up from eating rust-tainted food.

hazards.name: Woke-Bone Sickness
hazards.summary: The result of spending too long around the unearthed bones of Toothen Grove: sufferers become skeletal golems still clothed in the unwilling flesh of their erstwhile owners, screaming through jaws no longer under their control.

hazards.name: Glypher's Curse
hazards.summary: A spore-borne illness picked up by dredgers that grows in the brain, giving its host the ability to read and speak Highvin while robbing them of all other languages.

hazards.name: Ration-Mold
hazards.summary: A fungal mycosis from spoiled food whose spores progressively infect and overtake a host's faculties, turning them into a prisoner in their own body.

hazards.name: The Pyre
hazards.summary: A condition in which sufferers spontaneously burn from within, with fire behind their eyes; whether infection, side-effect, or curse, most simply call it the Pyre.

hazards.name: Whispering Lung
hazards.summary: A whisper-based affliction in which a whisper refuses to be driven out of the mind and takes refuge deeper in the body, stealing the sufferer's ability to speak.
